source.title: Do Mice Grok? Glimpses of Hidden Progress During Overtraining in Sensory Cortex
source.authors: Tanishq Kumar; Blake Bordelon; Cengiz Pehlevan; Venkatesh N. Murthy; Samuel Gershman

record.tranche_reason: The study tests grokking-like delayed generalization and hidden progress using a synthetic odor-classification task and a reanalysis of mouse neural data, rather than reproducing the original modular-arithmetic setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own synthetic-model and neural-data results. It also describes held-out odor performance from Berners-Lee et al. (2023), but that cited result is not recorded as a row. The neural reanalysis does not track held-out test accuracy throughout overtraining.
record.test_reason: The synthetic one-hidden-layer MLP on a constructed odor-classification task shows probe accuracy jumping well after training loss converges, with margin and Fisher discriminant rising gradually first. That is a new, non-algorithmic setting with its own result on V3 and, from the text, on V2. The mouse piriform reanalysis measures representational separation in biological cortex. It tracks no held-out accuracy during overtraining, so it is not the kind of system the versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find evidence of continued representation learning (class separation, margin growth) in mouse piriform cortex during overtraining, and a synthetic MLP reproduces grokking-like probe generalization through late-time margin maximization under cross-entropy. They also use a two-layer linear model to explain the overtraining reversal effect. They call the neural evidence observational and suggestive, not conclusive.
record.recipe_differences: The study reanalyzes mouse odor-discrimination recordings and trains synthetic odor-classification models, rather than using the original small modular-arithmetic training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: In the synthetic model, replacing cross-entropy with hinge loss causes margin and test loss to saturate around the time training loss does. Mouse S differs from the other mice in the reported representational-separation trend.

fits_no_version.finding: In mouse posterior piriform cortex, target/nontarget representations keep separating during behavioral overtraining. Decoding accuracy and SVM margins rise, except in Mouse S.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Biological sensory cortex shows hidden representational progress after behavior plateaus, analogous to grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Hinge loss stops margin growth when training loss saturates, tying late margin maximization to the cross-entropy objective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-time margin maximization under cross-entropy drives delayed generalization.

record.problems: The neural evidence is observational; only around 20 neurons are recorded per mouse-day; Mouse S does not follow the general anticorrelation trend; Mouse T has inconsistent late data that are dropped; the paper does not measure held-out generalization throughout neural overtraining.
record.rows_left_out: The mean-matched random-firing-rate comparison in Appendix A.5, Figure 8 is not included as a separate row; it is a control for representational separation, not a separate delayed-generalization outcome. No other relevant reported outcomes were omitted.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets; no variation of training-set size against delay.
No identified generalizing circuit, no Fourier features, no removal of memorizing components.
No images, text or molecules; initialization scale and weight norm are not varied (only the loss function is ablated).
No weight decay sweep, critical dataset size or ungrokking. The bio model is trained without weight decay.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.
No test of optimizer or floating-point artifacts (plain gradient descent is used).

missing.what: Classifier margin over training for the cross-entropy MLP, rising continuously after training loss plateaus
Fisher discriminant between target and probes over training, per overlap level, rising before and through the accuracy jump
Training and test loss curves for the cross-entropy MLP, with test loss falling after training loss plateaus

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new setting, not a different method on the original task. Mouse rows are unlinked because they concern biological cortex with no held-out accuracy tracked during overtraining. The synthetic probes are out-of-distribution, and the delay is shown only for a single constructed task. V2 support rests on figure-only progress measures that no row records.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test small algorithmic datasets such as modular arithmetic, or whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

It measures gradual representational separation, margins, and Fisher discriminant progress, but does not identify a specific generalizing circuit, show memorizing components being removed, or test Fourier features.
The study reports grokking-like delayed generalization in a synthetic odor task and neural data, but does not vary initialization scale or weight norm or test a lazy-to-rich switch caused by them.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test weight decay, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
The study does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax.

relationships.reason: Probe accuracy jumps abruptly during epochs 1000-9000, after training loss converged (R12-R16). Probe test loss keeps falling late in the bio model (R19, partial: loss only).
